game: MIN@DET Week 9 2025, kickoff 2025-11-02 13:00 ET, Ford Field dome, DET -9.5, total 47.5. Read stamped pre-kickoff morning; inactives (~90 min pre-kick) not in pack.

script.base: DET is laying 9.5 with a 28.5 implied total in a dome (total 47.5), so the Lions should lead by halftime and finish on the ground with Jahmyr Gibbs (46 carries, 255 yards in weeks 5-7) and David Montgomery. MIN's 19.0 implied total means Carson Wentz is chasing: pass volume to Justin Jefferson (32 targets, 276 yards, 368 air yards over weeks 5/7/8) and the run share for Jordan Mason (32 carries, 112 yards, 3.5 YPC in that same window) dies.
script.flip1: MIN hangs within one score because DET's 33% blitz does not bury Wentz (MIN EPA/db is -0.29 vs blitz but 0.00 clean) or Detroit turns it over. Mason keeps a full early-down load near his recent 52-57 rush-yard games and can clear 57.5, and both passing games stay live.
script.flip2: DET is up 17+ by half, clocks out, and Goff/Amon-Ra/Jameson Williams stall the way a favorite-up script stalls QB and WR yards. Gibbs and Montgomery carries spike until starters sit; MIN abandons the run entirely, and garbage throws tilt short to T.J. Hockenson (Josh Oliver is out) instead of deep to Jefferson.

injury_fallout: Sources: official pre-game injury report in the pack only; no practice-trend (DNP/limited/full) and no inactives. DET OUT: RB Craig Reynolds (hamstring) and RB Sione Vaki questionable (groin) push leftover carries to Gibbs and Montgomery; S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Daniel Thomas (forearm) out plus CB Avonte Maddox questionable (hamstring) and LB Malcolm Rodriguez out (knee) open deep and middle throws for Jefferson/Addison/Hockenson and slightly help MIN RBs (Rodriguez). LT Taylor Decker questionable (shoulder) would cut DET rush efficiency if he sits. MIN OUT: TE Josh Oliver (foot) funnels TE targets to Hockenson; FB C.J. Ham (hand) nicks the run game; CB Jeff Okudah (concussion) out and S Josh Metellus questionable (foot) help DET receivers, especially outside/deep (Jameson Williams) and the middle (LaPorta/ARSB); LB Andrew Van Ginkel questionable (neck) would lower MIN's 49% blitz pressure if inactive. Both MIN tackles, Brian O'Neill and Christian Darrisaw, are questionable (knee): if either is inactive, pressure up, Mason efficiency down, quick throws up, Jefferson/Addison deep yards down. Jefferson over 79.5 is the re-run leg only if both tackles are active; it is not on the card before inactives.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack (coverage charting not saved). Location proxy: DET allows 9.2 YPA in the middle (50 attempts) vs 6.81 left (90) and 5.68 right (98). MIN allows 12.18 YPA in the middle (45) vs 6.19 left (75) and 6.4 right (65).
matchup.pressure: DET blitzes 33%; MIN EPA/db is -0.29 when blitzed vs 0.00 when not, and that gets worse if O'Neill or Darrisaw sits. MIN blitzes 49%; Goff's EPA/db is +0.61 vs blitz and only +0.08 vs none. Van Ginkel questionable would soften that pressure.
matchup.bleeds: MIN run defense allows 4.41 YPC and 27 runs of 10+ (7 games) and is worst in the middle of the field (12.18 YPA); only 16 passes of 20+ (203 yards). DET run defense is tighter at 4.19 YPC and 20 runs of 10+, but has allowed 21 passes of 20+ (261 yards) and 9.2 YPA in the middle.
matchup.overlap: DET's primary target Amon-Ra St. Brown (29 targets, 231 yards, 197 air yards in weeks 5-7) and Sam LaPorta (15 targets, 162 yards, 73 air) attack the middle where MIN is worst, into a blitz Goff has crushed, with Okudah out. That overlap is real, but ARSB's 77.5 stand-in equals his recent ~77-yard pace, so it is not one of the two cards. The rush overlap used instead: Gibbs' lead-back share into MIN's 4.41 YPC / 27 explosive runs, in a -9.5 run-late script. MIN's primary, Jefferson, overlaps DET's missing safeties and 9.2 middle YPA, but only if the tackles protect.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. The game stayed inside one score, MIN never abandoned the run, and Mason's 57-yard games became 58-plus on one crease because Rodriguez was out. On the other side Montgomery took the grind (he already has a 65-yard game in the last four and 35 carries in the L3), Decker was limited, and Gibbs finished at 54 or 65 again while a single explosive was charted to someone else. The 67.5 and 57.5 rungs are season medians, so half a yard the wrong way was always the whole bet, and there was never a no-vig price to prove an edge.
slip_story: One story only: favorite runs the clock, dog abandons the run. Gibbs rush over and Mason rush under win together in the base and in flip 2. They are not a shootout stack. Do not add Jefferson, LaPorta, or ARSB overs to this slip; those need pass volume that flip 2 kills. Jefferson over 79.5 is the separate MIN-chase sleeper to re-run only if O'Neill and Darrisaw are active. No parlay is placed.
